request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Electronic Health Record: Discharge Summary

Patient Information:
Name: Anonymous
Gender: Male
Age: 63 years
Admission Date: [Date]
Discharge Date: [Date]

Reason for Admission:
The patient presented with a three-month history of dull epigastric pain radiating to the right hypochondrium and was diagnosed with mild gastritis. Ultrasonography revealed many gallstones with a thickened wall of the gall bladder. He was transferred to our center for an elective cholecystectomy.

Hospital Course:
The patient underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy, which revealed an empyema of the gallbladder with stones that made dissection difficult due to local inflammation. On the first day after the surgery, he complained of pain at the right hypochondrium and a decrease in hemoglobin. Computed tomography (CT) showed a perihepatic hematoma extending to the right paracolic gutter without evidence of any other neoplasm. The patient was monitored for seven weeks with follow-up CTs and ultrasound scans until a 19 mm hypodense nodule was discovered on the eighth liver segment. A fine needle aspiration (FNA) revealed that it was a metastatic signet-ring cell carcinoma. Several CTs and ultrasound scans were performed for surveillance until retroperitoneal and right axillary adenopathies, liver masses, peritoneal dissemination, subcutaneous nodules on the chest wall, and, at the entrance of the right laparoscopy trocar, were described as metastases 9 months later. The patient was placed on palliative care, which lasted for one month until his eventual death.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Disposition:
The patient was placed on palliative care and eventually died.

Follow-up:
N/A

Signed,
[Physician's Name and Title]

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The episode began as an elective admission for laparoscopic cholecystectomy because of gallstones with a thickened gallbladder wall. At surgery the gallbladder was found to have empyema with stones. The principal diagnosis is the condition established after study to be chiefly responsible for the admission, and here that is the cholelithiasis with empyema of the gallbladder. The later metastatic signet-ring cell carcinoma was found during follow-up, not as the reason for the elective admission.

The case is ambiguous because the primary of the metastatic signet-ring cell carcinoma is never identified, and the course ends in death. The task asks for the condition responsible for the episode of care, and the surgical admission was for the gallbladder disease.

Gallstones with acute cholecystitis, including empyema, fall under K80. Calculus of the gallbladder with acute cholecystitis is K80.0, and gallbladder empyema with calculus is classified to K80.0 or K80.1 depending on the coding. The category is K80 either way.

The alternative would be C80 or C78 for the cancer, but the cancer was not what the surgical admission was for.

CODE: K80
